get.summary: List the workspace's people, agents and runners, oldest first. Person token.

post.summary:
Mint an agent actor with its own token and no run. Its token reaches the workspace's
issues, `/api/issues/<id>` and below, and nothing else. Person token.

Receive a GitHub webhook delivery. The signature is checked, the payload parsed, and a
job queued to record it; the answer does not wait for the job. Unauthenticated: GitHub
signs the body instead of sending a bearer token.

202.description: Accepted: queued, or ignored because Punchlist does not record this event.

401.description: The signature is missing or wrong.

422.description: A required header is missing or the payload is malformed.

get.summary:
List the workspace's issues, oldest first, each with its run, newest pull request and
next gated transition's gates.

post.summary: Create an issue in the workflow's first status, and its `created` event.

get.summary: Show one issue.

patch.summary:
Edit an issue's title, body, labels, assignee, parent, project or milestone. Only the
fields that change are written, with one `edited` event naming them; a request that
changes nothing writes nothing and answers the workspace's latest sequence number. Nobody
in a role the issue's status locks may edit it.

403.description: An agent edited another issue than its run's.

409.description: The issue's status is locked to the actor's role.

422.description: An empty title, a bad label, an assignee that is not a person or agent of the workspace, a parent that is not an issue of the workspace or would make a cycle, a project or milestone that is not the workspace's, or a milestone outside the issue's project.

post.summary:
Comment on an issue. An agent's comment ends with `(agent)` on its own line. Nobody
in a role the issue's status locks may comment.

403.description: An agent commented on another issue than its run's.

409.description: The issue's status is locked to the actor's role.

get.summary: An issue's timeline, oldest first.

The gates of the issue's next gated transition, each checked against the evidence
recorded now. Nothing is read from GitHub and nothing is written: a request for the
transition reads GitHub first, so it can answer differently. 204 when no transition an
actor can request from the issue's status has gates.

204.description: The issue's status has no gated transition.

get.summary: An issue's proof, oldest first.

post.summary:
Attach a file to an issue as proof, in the issue's current attempt. Nobody in a role the
issue's status locks may attach proof, as for comments.

403.description: An agent attached proof to another issue than its run's.

409.description: The issue's status is locked to the actor's role, or its attempt changed while the file uploaded.

413.description: The file is over the server's limit.

422.description: No title or file, a content type proof cannot be, or a kind that is not the content type's.

get.summary: An issue's pull requests, newest number first.

post.summary:
An issue's pull requests and the unresolved review threads of the open ones, after
reading both from GitHub as a gated request does: a new review thread sends no webhook,
so this is how an agent reads what its reviewers wrote. The thread text is from outside
the team; only this route returns it. When GitHub cannot be read, or there is no GitHub
App, `refreshed` is false and the answer is what is recorded.

get.summary: An issue's runs, newest first.

The transitions that can be requested from the issue's status, each with the verdict the
caller's request would get: the same rules and gates `POST /api/issues/{id}/transitions`
checks, over the evidence recorded now. Nothing is read from GitHub and nothing is
written, so a request, which reads GitHub first, can still answer differently.

post.summary:
Move an issue to another status. The workflow's lock, role and gate rules are checked,
and the status, the transition, its gate results and its event are written, in one
transaction.

409.description: Refused; the message names the rule.

get.summary: List the workspace's projects, oldest first, each with its milestones, oldest first.

post.summary: Create a project in the workspace.

422.description: An empty or long name, or one the workspace already has.

post.summary: Create a milestone in one of the workspace's projects.

422.description: An empty or long name, or one the project already has.

get.summary:
A proof file's bytes, with its content type. It is served so that a browser neither
guesses another type nor runs it. An agent's token gets 403: agents reach only
`/api/issues/...`.

200.description: The file, with its stored content type.

get.summary: The workspace repository's pull requests that name no issue, newest number first.
List the workspace's runners, oldest first.

post.summary:
Register a runner. Needs a person's token. Creates the runner's own actor. A name this
person already registered in the workspace re-adopts the newest such runner instead: the
same id and actor, the request's agents, and a new token, so the old one stops working.
That is how a restarted runner keeps the attempts it holds (`GET /api/runners/{id}/leases`),
and why two runners started with one name cannot both run.

201.description: Registered, or re-adopted with a new token.

post.summary:
Record a heartbeat and renew the leases of the attempts the body lists as held. A running
attempt that is not listed, or whose lease already lapsed, is not renewed: it expires and
the sweep fails it. The answer lists the held attempts that were not renewed (`stale`),
so the runner stops their agents: the issue of one whose lease lapsed is dispatched again.
The body is optional; without it no lease is renewed. Runner token, for the runner's own
id only.

get.summary:
The running attempts the runner holds whose leases have not lapsed, oldest first. A
runner that restarts reads these: it resumes each one it can (`POST /api/runs/{id}/resume`)
and reports the rest lost. Read-only. Runner token, for the runner's own id only.

post.summary:
Claim an issue: one in Start, or one waiting in a status it entered whose dispatch rule
names an agent the runner can run. Runner token. 204 when nothing is claimable; with
`wait_seconds` the request waits for one. When several runners wait, each issue goes to
one of them and the others get 409 `claim_taken`.

409.description: Another runner claimed the issue first.

post.summary:
Record the outcome of the runner's running attempt and of its run. A lost attempt keeps
the run running for its next attempt while the run has one left (`settle_run`).

409.description: The attempt is not the runner's running attempt.

get.summary: Every log line of a run, oldest first.

post.summary: Append lines to a run's log. Only the runner holding the running attempt may write.

409.description: The attempt is not the runner's running attempt.

post.summary:
Resume the runner's running attempt after the runner restarted: renews its lease, gives
the run's agent a new token, and answers the attempt's claim again, with the same agent
session and the number of the attempt's next log line. No attempt is created. Runner
token; 409 `stale_attempt` unless the attempt is the runner's running attempt and its
lease has not lapsed.

409.description: The attempt is not the runner's running attempt.

get.summary: Who the request is signed in as, by its bearer token or its session cookie.

post.summary: Sign in with a person's token: the answer sets the session cookie to it.

delete.summary: Sign out: the answer clears the session cookie.

get.summary:
The workspace's active workflow: its version, the commit it came from, its statuses and
the last push that was refused.
The JSON Schema for `.punchlist/workflow.toml`. Unauthenticated, so editors can fetch it.

The workspace's events after `after`, as Server-Sent Events: each one's `id` is its
sequence number and its data a `StreamItem`, with the issue's row as it is when the
event is sent. The stream stays open.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
Stream the events after this sequence number: the list's `last_event_seq`. A
reconnecting `EventSource`'s `Last-Event-ID` takes its place.

200.description: One `issue` message per event, in sequence order.

get.summary:
What the workspace holds from Linear, counted from the rows with a Linear id, and its
latest import. Person token.

post.summary:
Import a Linear project, as `pl import linear` read it. Every issue's state must map to a
status of the active workflow, or nothing is queued. Person token.

422.description: A Linear state maps to no status; the message names each.

get.summary: One import of the workspace. Person token.

404.description: Not the token's workspace, or no such import in it.

kind.description: The agent key, such as `codex`. Only agents have one. Absent from an older server.

ActorInfo.description: An actor in the workspace: a person, an agent or a runner.

kind.description: The agent key. Only agents have one.

owner.description: The name of the person an agent acts for. Only agents have one.

first_line.description:
The 1-based number, within this attempt, of the first line in `lines`. The lines are
consecutive numbers from here. A resent batch keeps its `first_line`, so the server
stores each numbered line once. Gaps between batches are fine.

file.description: The file, with its content type on the part.

oneOf.description: Must be the kind of the file's content type, when given.

model.description: The model the runner passed the agent; `None` for the agent's default.

CheckRunEvidence.description: A check run on a pull request's head commit.

app.description:
The slug of the GitHub App that created the run, such as `github-actions`; absent for a
run recorded before apps were.

conclusion.description: Set once completed, such as `success` or `failure`.

workflow_default_sha.description:
The same path's blob on the default branch when the run was read; absent when the
default branch has no such file.

workflow_other_bases.description:
The branches other than the default branch that a pull request from the run's head
branch has been into, open or closed, earlier bases too. A pull request's run takes its
workflow file from the head commit merged into the base, and GitHub does not say which
pull request a run was for, so any of them may have run it. Empty when every one was
into the default branch; absent when no pull request from a branch of the workspace's
repository is behind the run, and whenever `workflow_path` is absent.

workflow_path.description:
The workflow file of the GitHub Actions job behind the run, such as
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, when a gated request's read of GitHub found one that a runner
took. Absent for another app's run, for a check run that no job ran (anything with
`checks: write` can create one of any name on any commit), for a job still waiting for
a runner, and for a run that only a delivery recorded.

workflow_sha.description: That file's blob at the head commit; absent when the commit has no such file.

ChecksState.description: The check runs on a pull request's head commit, taken together.

Claim.description:
A claimed issue, with the attempt leased to the runner. The server either moved it from
Start to In Progress as the runner, or it was waiting in a status it entered that has a
dispatch rule, such as Agent Review.

agent.description: The agent key from the dispatch rule, such as `claude-code`.

agent_token.description:
The bearer token of the agent actor this run acts as, for the MCP server. Valid
while the run is running, until the next claim or resume of the run replaces it.

attempt.description: The compare-and-set token for logs and the outcome.

branch.description:
The branch to work on, `feature/<id>`, or `feature/<id>-<n>` from the issue's second
lifecycle on.

issue.description: The issue, in the status whose dispatch rule the run is for.

merged_branches.description:
The issue's branches with a merged pull request and no open one, sorted. The runner
replaces a worktree it still has on one of them. Empty when no earlier branch of the
issue has merged.

next_line.description:
The number of the attempt's next log line: 1 on a fresh attempt, one past the last
stored line on a resumed one.

prompt.description: The workflow's prompt for the status: `prompts/system.md`, then the status's own.

session_id.description:
The attempt's agent session: `claude --session-id` on a fresh attempt, `--resume`
on a resumed one.

wait_seconds.description:
Wait up to this many seconds (at most 30) for an issue to become claimable before
answering 204.

CreateAgent.description:
`POST /api/actors`, with a person's token. Mints an agent actor that acts through its own
token, with no run.

owner.description:
The name of the person in the workspace the agent acts for. The requesting person by
default.

name.description: Trimmed, 1 to 100 characters, unique in the project.

pass_when.description: What must be true for the milestone to pass.

name.description: Trimmed, 1 to 100 characters, unique in the workspace.

token.description: The agent's bearer token. Shown once; only its hash is stored.

ErrorBody.description: The body of every error response.

code.description: A stable code, such as `role_not_allowed`, `gate_failed` or `not_found`.

oneOf.description: For `gate_failed`: what the gates read.

gate.description: For `gate_failed`: the first gate that failed.

message.description: What went wrong. For a refused transition, the rule that refused it.

reason.description:
For `gate_failed`: why that gate failed, as people read it: the gate result's `reason`
joined with the names in its `outside` (`GateResult::text()`), where the result's own
`reason` is the sentence only.

Event.description: One entry in an issue's timeline.

delivery_id.description:
The GitHub webhook delivery that caused the move, for moves made on a GitHub
event.

from_name.description: `from` as people read it, such as `In Progress`.

workflow_version.description: The content hash of the workflow the transition was checked against.

oneOf.description:
A comment on the issue, such as the one a pull request closed without merging
requires.

A transition that a GitHub event would have made and a gate refused. The issue
stayed in `from`.

delivery_id.description:
The GitHub webhook delivery that brought the event; absent when the server read
the pull request from GitHub itself.

from_name.description: `from` as people read it, such as `Merging`.

gate.description: The gate that failed, such as `proof_attached`.

workflow_version.description: The content hash of the workflow the transition was checked against.

oneOf.description:
A run of the issue was claimed or ended, or lost its attempt. This kind, `pull_request`,
`proof` and `workflow` say only that the issue's row changed: the event stream carries
them, and an issue's timeline leaves them out.

GitHub evidence on the issue's pull requests was recorded: a pull request, the check
runs on its head commit, or its review threads.
Proof was attached to the issue.

The workspace loaded a different workflow version, which can change the gates and status
names every row shows.

Evidence.description: What the gates read for one issue.

attempt.description: The issue's attempt: how many times it has moved from Start to In Progress.

closed_pull_request.description:
The pull request that a GitHub event merged or closed without merging, when that event
is causing the move; absent on a requested move, and read only by `pr_names_issue`.

proof.description: The proof attached to the issue, from every attempt.

pull_requests.description: The pull requests linked to the issue, open or not.

lost.description:
The runner lost the attempt before its agent finished, such as when it stopped or
restarted. Only with `failed`. A lost attempt that is not the run's last allowed one
keeps the run running for another attempt.

reason.description: Why the attempt failed. Required when the outcome is `failed`.

GateChecklist.description:
`GET /api/issues/{id}/gates`: the gates an issue has to pass for its next gated
transition, each checked against the evidence recorded now.

to.description: The status the gated transition moves to.

GateResult.description:
One gate's result. `reason` says why it passed or failed, in Punchlist's own words: every
name in it is a number, an issue id or one of GitHub's own words. What GitHub's users named
is in `outside`, so an agent's tools can show that as data and the reason as Punchlist's.
`reason` is therefore the sentence only; `text()` is the whole of it, and is what
`ErrorBody.reason`, the refusal's message and the stored rows hold.

outside.description:
The text from outside the team that the reason is about, one entry per thing: the
failed checks' names, the open threads' files. At most five, each cut short.

outside_more.description: How many more there are than `outside` names.

GateSummary.description: The gates of the issue's next gated transition, over the evidence recorded now.

first_failed.description: The first gate that fails, in the workflow's order.

to.description: The status the gated transition moves to.

held.description:
The attempts the runner is working on. Only these leases are renewed; any other
running attempt of this runner expires and the sweep fails it.

stale.description:
The attempts in `held` that are not this runner's running attempts any more: finished,
or failed when the lease lapsed. The issue may already have another run, so the runner
stops their agents.

HeartbeatReply.description: The response to `POST /api/runners/{id}/heartbeat`: the runner, and what it must stop.

HeldAttempt.description: An attempt a runner is working on.

notes.description: Issues gone from Linear's project, parents outside it, empty comments skipped.

ImportRun.description: One import, as the server's job runs it.

error.description: Why the last attempt failed; a `queued` import with one is retried.

oneOf.description: Set once it is `done`.

ImportStatus.description:
`GET /api/workspaces/{id}/imports`: the workspace's rows imported from Linear, and the
latest import.

oneOf.description: A person or an agent; `None` when nobody is assigned.

id.description: The identifier people use, such as `PL-1`.

labels.description: In the order they were set.

oneOf.description: The Linear issue it was imported from; `None` for an issue made in Punchlist.
One of `project`'s milestones.

parent.description: The parent issue's id, such as `PL-1`; `None` when the issue has none.

status.description: The workflow's status key, such as `in_progress`.

status_name.description: The status as people read it, such as `In Progress`.

last_event_seq.description:
The sequence number of the workspace's latest event, read in the same snapshot as
the list (ADR 0006).

IssueRow.description:
An issue as the list and the board show it: the issue, its run, its newest pull request
and its next gated transition's gates.

oneOf.description: `None` when no transition an actor can request from the issue's status has gates.
The issue's highest-numbered pull request; `None` when none is linked.

IssueWritten.description:
The answer to a write: the changed issue's row and the sequence number of the event it
recorded, or the workspace's latest when it recorded none (ADR 0006). The client drops
that event when the stream delivers it.

Lease.description:
`GET /api/runners/{id}/leases`: a running attempt the runner holds whose lease has not
lapsed. A runner that restarts resumes or fails each one.

repository.description: Where the issue's worktree is cloned from.

oneOf.description: `None` for a comment an integration wrote.

LinearImport.description:
`POST /api/workspaces/{id}/imports/linear`: one Linear project as `pl import linear` read
it. Every id is Linear's, and a rerun finds what it imported before by them.

description.description: Imported as the milestone's PASS when text.

seq.description: Increases per run, in the order the server received the lines.

pass_when.description: What must be true for the milestone to pass; empty when nobody wrote it.

to.description: The status key to move to, such as `todo`.

Moved.description: A transition that the server accepted.

warning.description:
Set when the move put the issue in Start under an active workflow version that fails
validation, so no runner can claim it: the validation problem.

Proof.description: A file attached to an issue as proof of its work.

attempt.description:
The issue's attempt when it was uploaded: how many times the issue had moved from
Start to In Progress.

title.description: What it shows, in its uploader's words.

ProofEvidence.description: A proof record attached to the issue.

attempt.description: The issue's attempt when it was uploaded.

PullRequest.description:
A pull request on the workspace's repository, as recorded from GitHub's events.
`GET /api/issues/{id}/pull-requests` and `GET /api/pull-requests/unlinked` return these.

check_runs.description:
The newest check run of each name on the head commit, as `ci_green` reads them. Only
an issue's pull requests carry them; their names are text from outside the team.

checks_total.description: Check runs on the head commit, and how many of them passed.

issue_id.description: The issue the branch or title names; `None` when it is unlinked.

PullRequestEvidence.description: A pull request linked to the issue, as GitHub's events recorded it.

check_runs.description:
The check runs on the head commit, the newest of each name. Read for an open pull
request.

merge_state.description:
GitHub's `mergeable_state`, such as `clean` or `dirty`; `unknown` until GitHub has
computed it.

review_threads.description: Its review threads, resolved or not. Read for an open pull request.

PullRequestState.description: A pull request's state on GitHub.

PullRequestStatus.description: A pull request's state as people read it: `draft` is an open draft.

url.description: `None` unless it is a plain `https://github.com/<owner>/<name>/pull/<number>` URL.

PullRequestsNow.description:
`POST /api/issues/{id}/pull-requests/refresh`: the issue's pull requests and what their
reviewers wrote, after reading both from GitHub.

refreshed.description:
False when GitHub could not be read, or the server has no GitHub App: the rest is
then what was last recorded.

review_threads.description: The unresolved review threads of the open ones.

RegisterRunner.description:
`POST /api/runners`, with a person's token. Registers a runner and creates its actor, or
re-adopts the runner this person registered under the same name, with a new token.

agents.description: Agent keys the runner can start, such as `claude-code`.

models.description:
The model the runner passes each agent, by agent key, such as `claude-code` →
`haiku`. An agent missing here runs its own default model.

name.description: A name people read, such as `sartre`.

lease_seconds.description: How long a lease lasts without a heartbeat.

token.description:
The runner actor's bearer token, for heartbeats, claims, logs and outcomes. Shown
once; only its hash is stored.

ResumeRun.description:
`POST /api/runs/{id}/resume`: the attempt the runner still holds, to run again in the
same agent session.

ReviewThread.description: An unresolved review thread. Its path, authors and bodies are text from outside the team.

comments.description: The thread's newest comments, oldest first.

comments_total.description: How many comments the thread has, which can be more than `comments`.

id.description: GitHub's node id for the thread, which its reply and resolve mutations take.

line.description: The line the thread is on, or was on before the file changed under it.

pull_request.description: The number of the pull request it is on.

ReviewThreadEvidence.description: A review thread on a pull request.

line.description: The line it is on, or was on before the file changed under it.

path.description: The file it is on; absent for a thread recorded before paths were.

Run.description: A run and its latest attempt. `GET /api/issues/{id}/runs` returns these, newest first.

agent_name.description: The agent as people read it, such as `Claude Code`.

attempt.description: The latest attempt's number, runner, failure reason, duration and tokens.

log_tail.description: The last 20 log lines, oldest first.

model.description: The model the latest attempt's runner passed the agent; `None` for the agent's default.

oneOf.description: No run is running or waiting, and the last one in this status did not fail.
A dispatch waits for a runner that can run `agent`.
The latest run in the issue's status failed.

RunSummary.description: What the issue's agent is doing in its status.

Session.description: Who a request is signed in as.

closed.description: No transition leaves it, as with Done and Canceled. The list hides these by default.

dispatch.description: The agent a runner starts when an issue enters it, such as `claude-code`.

locked_to.description: The roles that may not act on an issue in it, from the workflow's `[lock]`.

name.description: As people read it, such as `In Progress`.

StreamItem.description:
One message of `GET /api/workspaces/{id}/events`: an event and its issue's row as it is
now, which can be newer than the event.

TransitionList.description:
`GET /api/issues/{id}/transitions`: the moves that can be requested from the issue's
status, each with the verdict the caller's request would get on the evidence recorded now.

status.description: The issue's status; `locked_to` are the roles it locks out.

transitions.description: Each transition from `status` that is not made only by an event, in the workflow's order.

viewer_locked.description: The status locks the caller's role out: it can move, comment on and edit nothing here.

UpdateIssue.description: `PATCH /api/issues/{id}`. An absent field is left as it is.

assignee.description: A person's or an agent's actor id, or `null` to unassign.

labels.description: Each trimmed, 1 to 50 characters; at most 20, duplicates dropped.

milestone.description: A milestone of the project the issue has after the edit, or `null` for none.

parent.description:
An issue id of the workspace, such as `PL-1`, or `null` for none. Neither the issue
itself nor one of the issues under it.

project.description:
A project's id, or `null` for none. A change of project clears the milestone, unless
the same request sets one.

oneOf.description: The issue would move.
The first gate that fails (`gate_failed`).

The workflow refuses the caller: `code` is the refusal's, such as `locked` or
`role_not_allowed`, and `message` names the rule.

Verdict.description:
What `POST /api/issues/{id}/transitions` would answer the caller, without the read of
GitHub a gated request makes first, so a request can still answer differently.

commit_sha.description: The default branch commit it was loaded from; `None` for the built-in workflow.

invalid.description:
Why a push of this version would be refused today: the line, the key and the
problem. The version stays in force until a valid file is pushed. `None` when valid.

oneOf.description: The last push of `workflow.toml` that was refused; `None` once a later load succeeds.

version.description: The content hash recorded on every transition.

WorkflowRefusal.description: A pushed `workflow.toml` the server refused to load.

commit_sha.description: The default branch commit that was refused.

reason.description: Why, as logged: the line and key, or the statuses still in use.
